headline: Why Your New Door Installation Might Be Lagging
articleBody: Getting new doors for your home should be exciting, but sometimes the process can feel like it's moving at a snail's pace. A big reason for delays often comes down to unforeseen structural issues once the old door is removed. Maybe there's some wood rot around the frame, or the opening isn't quite plumb. These aren't always visible until demolition starts. Another common holdup is special orders; custom sizes, unique materials, or specific finishes can add weeks, or even months, to the timeline because they're not stocked locally. Don't forget about permitting, especially for larger patio doors or structural changes, as this process can vary widely by local building department in Southern California and might take longer than anticipated. Incorrect measurements or a mismatch between the chosen door and the existing frame can also cause frustrating setbacks, requiring reorders or significant adjustments. It’s important to work with professionals who can foresee these issues and manage expectations from the get-go. For instance, our team at Affordable Home Remodeling, with over 40 years of combined experience, has seen it all and can help navigate these complexities, ensuring your door project stays on track as much as possible. A good contractor will communicate any potential delays transparently and offer solutions.
